title: Scott signs 'sore loser' bill for primary elections - NewsBreak
text: MONTPELIER, Vt. ( ABC22/FOX44 ) – In addition to a tax reform bill aimed at aiding veterans and families , Vermont Governor Phil Scott on Wednesday signed House Bill 474, which immediately prohibits candidates who lose primary elections from changing parties to run in the subsequent general election. In some cases, candidates who have lost major party primaries have won by running as independent candidates, or have run on third-party tickets. Former Connecticut Sen. Joe Lieberman won re-election in 2006 as an independent after losing to Ned Lamont in the Democratic primary. This law would not have affected cases such as that of Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), who won re-election via a write-in campaign after narrowly losing the Republican primary to Joe Miller in 2010. However, H. 474 does add an additional requirement for write-in candidates, who are now required to file a form to have votes listed in a primary election. However, if the number of write-in votes in an election is greater than the number of votes for the apparent winner, all write-in votes will be counted regardless. Scott, who is widely viewed as a moderate Republican, has occasionally faced primary challenges for the governor’s seat, but has won most of them by wide margins. In his closest primary race in 2016, he won over 60% of the vote. H. 474 also makes various changes to election deadlines, and clarifies that drivers license applications will only double as voter registration forms when the applicant attests to being a U.S. citizen. An earlier version of the bill directed Vermont’s secretary of state to explore using ranked-choice voting in presidential primaries, but that provision did not make it into the final version. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to ABC22 & FOX44.
